The '''2026 Watford Borough Council election''' was held on 7 May 2026, alongside the [[2026 United Kingdom local elections|other local elections across the United Kingdom]] held on the same day, to elect 12 of 36 members of [[Watford Borough Council]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Watford mayor says local elections should go ahead in 2026 |url=https://www.watfordobserver.co.uk/news/25710812.watford-mayor-says-local-elections-go-ahead-2026/ |date=19 December 2025 |access-date=29 January 2026 |publisher=[[Watford Observer]]}}</ref> The election was held alongside the [[2026 Watford mayoral election]].

Due to ongoing [[Upcoming structural changes to local government in England|local government reorganisation]], this was the final election to Watford Borough Council before it is abolished and replaced by a successor [[unitary authority]]. Elections to the successor authority are due to take place in 2027. In the election, the [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] won all 12 seats, including two gains from the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]], and maintained control of the council.<ref name="CleanSweep">{{cite web |last1=Fitzpatrick |first1=Liam |title=Watford local election result 2026 - Lib Dem clean sweep |url=https://www.watfordobserver.co.uk/news/26091599.watford-local-election-result-2026---lib-dem-clean-sweep/ |publisher=[[Watford Observer]] |access-date=9 May 2026 |date=8 May 2026}}</ref>

==Background==
In the [[2024 Watford Borough Council election|2024 local elections]], the [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] won 11 of the 12 seats up for election, including three seats gained from the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]], who held their leader's seat of Holywell.<ref name="2024LocalResults">{{Cite web |title=Watford result - Local Elections 2024 |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/election/2024/england/councils/E07000103 |date=3 May 2024 |access-date=29 January 2026 |publisher=[[BBC News]]}}</ref> With their election win, the Liberal Democrats maintained their 21-year control of the council.<ref name="2024LocalResults" /><ref name="2024LEResultsWO">{{cite web |last1=Roberts |first1=Gabriel |title=Watford Borough Council local election results in full |url=https://www.watfordobserver.co.uk/news/24297488.watford-borough-council-local-election-results-full/ |publisher=[[Watford Observer]] |access-date=17 February 2026 |date=3 May 2024}}</ref> In the [[2024 United Kingdom general election|2024 general election]], the Labour Party candidate [[Matt Turmaine]] gained the [[Watford (UK Parliament constituency)|Watford]] constituency from the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] incumbent [[Dean Russell]].<ref name="2024GEResults">{{cite web |title=Watford - General election results 2024 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/election/2024/uk/constituencies/E14001568 |publisher=[[BBC News]] |access-date=17 February 2026 |date=5 July 2024}}</ref> In January 2026, the council was given the option to cancel the 2026 elections in preparation for [[Upcoming structural changes to local government in England|local government reorganisation]], however, the council decided to proceed with the elections to "allow residents the right to exercise their democratic rights".<ref>{{cite web |title=Council - Tuesday, 27 January 2026 printed draft minutes |url=https://watford.moderngov.co.uk/documents/g5099/Public%20minutes%20Tuesday%2027-Jan-2026%2019.30%20Council.pdf |publisher=[[Watford Borough Council]] |access-date=17 February 2026 |page=18 |date=27 January 2026}}</ref>

Three [[by-election]]s were held between the 2024 and 2026 elections:
